episode_title: EP 242: Reflecting on the Gold Standard Retreat

real_qa.q: What is the 90-10 rule in leadership that John Harbaugh applies with the New York Giants?
real_qa.r: John Harbaugh's 90-10 rule focuses 90 percent of managerial attention on the 90 percent of things an employee does really well, giving them praise and positioning them to utilize their strengths, while reserving 10 percent of attention for critical feedback on areas needing improvement. This approach creates an environment where employees trust leadership enough to accept coaching and raise their own standards, as exemplified by Ray Lewis who would ask to be coached harder because the positive foundation was so strong.

real_qa.q: What specific content strategy did Bobby Maximus recommend for social media growth?
real_qa.r: Bobby Maximus recommended shooting 100 long-form videos within one year on subjects you know more about than the common person, then plugging them into Opus to chop them up into 15 or 20 short-form videos and posting every day. Long-form for social media means anything longer than five minutes focused on your specific expertise, whether that's combine coaching or weight loss specialization.
real_qa.requete: Bobby Maximus 100 long form videos strategy

real_qa.q: What communication principle did Jenny emphasize about clarity in client consultations?
real_qa.r: Jenny emphasized that the more you say, the more you have to explain, and recommended filtering communication through four questions: Does this need to be said? Is this kind? Does it add any value? And is it true? She also stated that clarity is kindness and that bottom lines focus minds, particularly on sales sheets and in knee-to-knee consulting opportunities where practitioners should answer the actual questions being asked rather than drifting.

real_qa.q: Why did the Business of Strength retreat move from holding Gym of the Year awards on day one to day two?
real_qa.r: The organizers strategically moved Gym of the Year ceremonies from day one to day two and thinned out presentations and lengthened breaks because in the previous year at Scottsville, they packed too much content on day two and observed people sleeping in the crowd after being gassed out on day one. The bar social on night one also takes a toll on attendees for the following day.
real_qa.requete: Business of Strength retreat schedule changes

real_qa.q: What did Tony Smith teach about reframing focus after setbacks through his son's baseball example?
real_qa.r: Tony Smith described how his son recalibrates after a strikeout by running back to the dugout and immediately cheering for the next batter, demonstrating that you cannot be negative and positive at the same time. This principle applies to business too—when marketing campaigns fail or team conversations go poorly, doing something to gain positive momentum like completing an effective workout or sending another marketing email is the best cure for negativity.
real_qa.requete: can't be negative and positive at same time

real_qa.q: What standard did Adam emphasize about knowing versus enforcing gym business protocols?
real_qa.r: Adam stated that knowing your standards and enforcing them are two different things. He emphasized that gym owners need to have team members walk lockstep by getting their hands dirty and showing them what a professional consult, exercise execution, and session setup and breakdown actually look like, referencing how the Blue Angels perform walkthroughs before every flight despite extensive training.
